newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Fuel oil stable, LSWR softer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Fuel oil stable, LSWR softer.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was stable on Tuesday as traders said the market is directionless at present with low trading interest.
Fuel oil 380-cst grade was bid at around Monday's level while the 180-cst grade was offered down, traders said.
The 380-cst grade was bid at $97 per tonne for August 19-23 lifting, while the 180-cst grade was offered at $99.5 for August 24-28, down from Monday's offer at $101.00.
Late last week, 180-cst grade was bid at $99 per tonne and the 380-cst was bid at $97.
"Some majors still have 180-cst cargoes for August but it seems interest is more on the 380-cst grade," said one trader, noting upward bunker levels.
The Singapore bunker market firmed due to month-end berth congestion and bunker traders expected firm levels to continue in the short term.
On the demand side, state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) issued a tender to buy 80,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil for September delivery.
The tender, which seeks 6,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur and 74,000 tonnes of 2.0-percent fuel oil for delivery September 1-10, closes on July 30 and is valid until July 31.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, traders said sentiment was not as firm as in the past few weeks as supplies from Indonesia for August were higher than those in July.
Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina allocated a total of 2.7 million barrels of LSWR for August lifting.
The allocation compared with the initial allocation of 2.3 million barrels in July, with additional 300,000 barrels rolled over from June.
In the face of higher supplies, offers for August 19-23 delivery free-on-board Indonesia fell to $16.00 per barrel from an earlier $16.50 but bids were scarce.
